points.t: Fixed **‘target’ lesions with three zones** on palms, backs of hands, forearms or feet, often **1–3 weeks after a cold sore**.
**Cell-mediated reaction to HSV antigen** in the skin (most cases); *Mycoplasma* in children; drugs uncommon.
Supportive care, potent topical steroid, mouthwashes, analgesia; aciclovir for active HSV; suppressive antiviral for recurrent HSV-EM (specialist).
**SJS / TEN**: atypical flat dusky targets, widespread skin pain, blistering and mucosal erosions after a new drug.

cause.lead: A type IV reaction to an infection.
points: **HSV-1 / 2** leads (1–3 weeks after herpes labialis / genitalis; recurs with HSV).
*Mycoplasma pneumoniae* in children / young adults with a respiratory prodrome.
Cytotoxic T cells attack keratinocytes → **epidermal necrosis in the target centre**.
**EM minor** = skin only; **EM major** = skin + ≥ 1 mucosa; still infection-related and **not** SJS / TEN.

visuals.caption: Typical target: dusky or blistered centre, pale oedematous ring, outer red ring with a sharp edge. Three zones point to EM; flat two-zone dusky macules point to SJS / TEN.
visuals.alt: Target lesion with three concentric zones

points: **Three zones**: dusky / purpuric or blistered centre → pale oedematous ring → red outer ring.
**Symmetrical, acral**: dorsal hands / feet, palms, extensor limbs, then trunk; face possible.
Mucosa: **oral erosions**, crusted lips (EM major); eyes / genitals less often.
Appear over days, resolve in **1–4 weeks**; recur with HSV.
Skin of colour: rely on zone architecture and palpation.

visuals.caption: EM favours the hands: symmetrical target lesions on the palms and backs of the hands.
visuals.alt: Palm and back of hand with scattered target lesions

points: Recent cold sore, respiratory symptoms, **new drugs**, mucosal / eye symptoms.
*Mycoplasma* testing, HSV swab of cold sore, biopsy.

cards.name: SJS / TEN
cards.clue: Flat atypical targets, widespread purpuric macules, sheet-like detachment; **drugs**; very unwell.

cards.name: Urticaria / urticaria multiforme
cards.clue: Migratory wheals < 24 h; no fixed dusky centre.

cards.name: Fixed drug eruption
cards.clue: Round dusky plaque recurring at the same site.

points: Emollients; soft diet and antiseptic / analgesic mouth rinses for oral EM; analgesia; rest.
Document drug history; stop a newly started suspect drug pending advice if morphology atypical.
**Potent topical steroid** to itchy / inflamed skin lesions.
Treat an active cold sore (topical / oral antiviral per BNF).
**Continuous or intermittent oral antiviral prophylaxis** (e.g. aciclovir): specialist / experienced initiation.
Systemic steroids only in selected severe cases under dermatology.

limits.t: Don’t start for presumed EM without specialist advice.

items.t: Mucosal erosions with **skin pain, blistering or skin loss**: possible **SJS / TEN**; stop suspect drugs, admit same day.
Unable to eat or drink: admission for fluids and analgesia.

pearls.t: **Raised three-zone targets on hands after a cold sore = EM. Flat dusky macules on the trunk after a new drug = SJS / TEN.**
Early antiviral for prodromal HSV may cut EM recurrences (individualise).
Mucosal involvement alone doesn’t make it SJS.
Scars are uncommon; pigment change can linger.

quiz.q: Three zones of a typical target?
quiz.a: Dusky / blistered centre, pale oedematous ring, red outer ring.
